name: Question 10
worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =0$ and $\sigma =6.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 12.18) & =P(Z\ge \frac{12.18-0}{6}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 2.03)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/c7af386057d2fba19697c0ad87c93a1865c69efaa1a5134f50bff6c7b9143dbe.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 2.03) & =1-P(Z<2.03) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 2.03) \\  & =1-Φ(2.03)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(2.03)=0.9788.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 2.03) & =1-Φ(2.03) \\  & =1-0.9788 \\  & =0.0212.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge 12.18)=0.0212.
$$

EXPLANATION

Given a normal random variable Y∼N(μ,σ2), we have

P(Y≥y)=P(Z≥y−μσ)

where Z∼N(0,1) is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have μ=0 and σ=6.

First, we transform Y into a standard normal random variable Z by z-scoring:

P(Y≥12.18)=P(Z≥12.18−06)=P(Z≥2.03)

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of Φ(z):

P(Z≥2.03)=1−P(Z<2.03)=1−P(Z≤2.03)=1−Φ(2.03)

From the table, we know that

Φ(2.03)=0.9788.

Therefore, we have

P(Z≥2.03)=1−Φ(2.03)=1−0.9788=0.0212.

Finally, we conclude that

P(Y≥12.18)=0.0212.
